theme: wildcard: a payments and consumer-credit analyst who knows public card
ideas: 1. BNPL loan-performance / delinquency disclosures (Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay ABS trust data, CFPB BNPL market monitoring) — tests the RNPL cancellation-risk thesis directly.

2. Card-linked consumer spend panels (Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker, central-bank card-spend series) broken out by travel/accommodation/restaurant category — near-real-time consumer strength by region.
3. CFPB Consumer Complaint Database (travel, lodging, prepaid-card, BNPL complaint categories) as a friction/cancellation-rate proxy.
4. Central-bank real-time card-spend indicators outside the US (Banco de Espana, Banco de Portugal, Norges Bank/SSB Norway, Danmarks Nationalbank) — regional consumer-strength split for EMEA mix.
5. Chargeback / dispute rate datasets or MCC-level spend indices (merchant-category-code panels) — take-rate and refund/cancellation friction proxy.
6. FinTech aggregator transaction panels (Plaid-based academic replication datasets, Yodlee panels used in papers) categorized by travel/lodging merchant.
7. Remittance price / cross-border money-transfer volume data (World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide) — cross-border consumer spending power proxy for LatAm/APAC regional mix.
8. NY Fed / Equifax Consumer Credit Panel (Household Debt and Credit Report) replication tooling — revolving credit utilization as a discretionary-travel-spend leading indicator.
9. Prepaid / gift-card balance and redemption trackers — discretionary spend proxy correlated with lodging/travel bookings.
10. Klarna/Affirm 'state of shopping' or BNPL adoption-by-category open datasets (travel vertical specifically) — RNPL adoption base rate outside Airbnb's own disclosures.

candidates.name: OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-download repo for the Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker (tracktherecovery.org): county/state/industry-level series including card spending by merchant category (restaurants, travel, retail, general merchandise), employment, and job postings, built from Affinity Solutions card-transaction data and other private-sector feeds. Aggregated/de-identified, updated on an ongoing basis (1,892+ commits, last touched 12 Sep 2026), CSV/dta files with a documented codebook. Requires citation of both the paper and data providers; no explicit OSS license stated.
candidates.why_useful: This is the exact 'Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker card spend' source named as a HIGH-value gap-6 target in CONTEXT.md — the GitHub repo is the actual pull mechanism (raw CSVs + codebook) rather than just the website, and its travel/restaurant spend-by-county series is a plausible near-real-time regional consumer-strength nowcast input for NA nights/ADR.
candidates.time_coverage: 2020-present, daily/weekly granularity, still updating in Sep 2026
candidates.size_hint: multiple CSV/dta files, tens of MB total across categories
candidates.license: none declared (custom attribution requirement, not a standard OSS license)

candidates.name: worldbank/RemittancePricesWorldwide
candidates.what_it_holds: World Bank's official repo mirroring the Remittance Prices Worldwide database (cost of sending remittances between country corridors). Content details (formats, exact time span) not confirmed beyond the repo landing page — README/data files need a follow-up pull; page shows a single initial commit as of Nov 2024.
candidates.why_useful: Remittance cost/flow data is a proxy for cross-border consumer purchasing power and outbound travel propensity in LatAm/APAC corridors — could support regional mix (LatAm/APAC) reads that CONTEXT.md gap #7 flags as thin; needs a closer look to confirm it is more than a stub.
candidates.time_coverage: unconfirmed — likely 2011-present per the public RPW series, needs verification inside the repo
candidates.size_hint: unconfirmed, appears to be a small/stub repo (1 commit)
candidates.license: not declared on the repo page

candidates.name: cfpb/ccdb5-ui
candidates.what_it_holds: Official CFPB GitHub org's front-end (JavaScript) for the Consumer Complaint Database search UI (consumerfinance.gov/complaint database), not the bulk data itself; the underlying complaint records (including travel/lodging, prepaid card, and BNPL complaint categories, since 2011, with company response and product/sub-product tags) are pulled separately via the CFPB's own Socrata-style bulk CSV/API, which this UI queries. Actively maintained (7 stars, updated 11 Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: The underlying complaint database (once pulled via the public API this UI hits) could give a free, point-in-time-taggable proxy for lodging-booking friction, cancellation disputes, and BNPL/prepaid-card complaint volume relevant to the RNPL thesis; this repo is only the client, so it is cataloged as a method/pointer, not a dataset — a follow-up agent should locate the actual bulk-export endpoint or a mirror repo of the CSV dumps.
candidates.time_coverage: 2011-present (underlying database), UI repo itself has no data
candidates.license: not confirmed (CFPB repos are typically CC0/public domain)
